STEP 1 - Scene: A snack/breakfast-type tray: two savory muffins (looks like cheese/ham/herb muffins in paper cases) on a white paper plate, with a latte in a white ceramic mug. The tray and cup are on an airplane-style table.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White paper plate, roughly 18 cm diameter (side-plate scale). Area = 3.14 x (9)^2 ≈ 254 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) two muffins in paper liners, (b) the latte (drink, not part of the solid meal estimate but noted).

STEP 4 - Area: Muffins together cover roughly 40% of the plate area (one large muffin ~20%, second ~15%, partly overlapping). Latte is off-plate, so excluded.

STEP 5 - Volume: Muffin 1: ~50 cm^2 footprint x ~5 cm height ≈ 250 ml envelope. Muffin 2: ~38 cm^2 x ~4 cm ≈ 150 ml envelope. Total ≈ 400 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Baked muffin, bread-like density ~0.5 g/ml given the domed, airy crumb and paper liner volume is included in the envelope. 400 ml x 0.5 ≈ 200 g. Using a 0.45 bulk factor gives about 180 g; I'll take ~180 g for the muffins.

STEP 7 - Energy: Savory muffin (cheese/ham style, baked with flour, egg, fat) ~350 kcal per 100 g. 180 g x 3.5 = ~630 kcal. Hmm, that's high for two small muffins; a more plausible figure for two muffins of this size is ~150 g at ~330 kcal/100 g ≈ 500 kcal. I'll use 150 g.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two medium savory muffins (~75 g each) are a plausible total of about 150 g and roughly 500 kcal. Latte is excluded from the solid estimate, though it adds roughly 100–150 kcal if counted.
